 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE PRAYING TO PERMIT THE PETITIONERS TO ACCEPT THE PACKAGE COMPENSATION OFFERED BY BMRCL / KIADB VIDE ANNEXURE A AND A1 UNDER SECTION 29(2) OF THE KIADB ACT WITH ACCRUED INTEREST TILL DATE OF PAYMENT TO THE PETITIONERS AND ETC.
 THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2023:KHC:21141  WP No. 11878 of 2023  ORDER
The petitioners in the present petition have sought for issuance of writ of certiorari to quash the General Award at Annexures-'G' and 'G1' dated 11.09.2018.

Further, the petitioners have sought for appropriate direction to enable them to accept the Package compensation offered by Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL)/Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB)
as per Annexures- 'A' and 'A1' under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 ('KIAD Act' for brevity) alongwith the accrued interest.
The petitioners have also sought for necessary direction to the respondents to deposit the balance amount in terms of Package compensation under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act before the Reference Court.

The petitioners have further sought for a direction that in the event, the petitioners succeed in the reference NC:
2023:KHC:21141 proceedings, i.e. in LAC No.67/2022 and LAC No. 126/ 2022 before the Reference Court, the petitioners would be entitled to the Package compensation that is to be deposited alongwith accrued interest.

The petitioners have also sought for refund of entire TDS amount deducted by providing the benefit under Section 96 of the New Act, 2023 (The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013)
with a further direction to the respondents not to deduct any amount in respect of balance

sentences.text:
The petitioners are stated to be the owners of the land bearing Survey No.87 of Kothanur Village,
Bangalore South Taluk.
The petitioners state that the land in Survey No.87 was proposed to be acquired by KIADB for the construction of Kothanur DEPO 2nd Stage Bangalore Metro Rail Project.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Preliminary NC: 2023:KHC:21141 Notification under section 28(1) and Final Notification under Section 28(4) of KIAD Act were issued notifying the Schedule Property.

3. It is submitted that suo motu proceedings were initiated under Rule 108-K of the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966 in LND RA(S) 18/16-17 in order to cancel the grant made and delete the names of the owners of the land from the revenue records, which though came to be allowed on 26.05.2017,
the same came to be challenged in W.P.No.26244/2017 c/w W.P.No. 25877/2017 filed by the other land owners.
The said Writ Petitions came to be allowed and the orders of Assistant Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner came to be set aside by order dated 07.02.2022.
The Court while disposing of the said Writ Petitions had directed the Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB to refer the dispute under Sections 30 and 31 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Subsequently, it is borne out from the facts that the Special Land Acquisition Officer-2, Metro, KIADB has filed Reference vide LAC No.67/2022 in respect of Schedule 'A'
property and LAC No.126/2022 in respect of Schedule 'B' property, which are pending before the City Civil Court, Bangalore (CCH-17).
4.

It is submitted that, though the amount that was deposited in LAC Nos.67/2022 and 126/2022 is in respect of General Award, however, in an identical factual matrix, i.e. in W.P.No.7752/2020 (LA-KIADB) this Court while disposing of the matter had directed KIADB to deposit the package amount of compensation in terms of Section 29(2) of KIAD Act.
5. Perused the order dated 08.12.2022 passed in W.P.No.7752/2020.
It is clear that the Reference Petitions pending before the Reference Court are now to be disposed off.

Insofar as the request by the NC: 2023:KHC:21141 petitioners for package amount of compensation in terms of Section 29(2),
it is to be noticed that, if the petitioners are found to be entitled in the reference proceedings to the compensation and their rights are determined, the proposal of petitioners for package compensation in terms of Section 29(2) would then require to be accepted.

If, after the culmination of Reference proceedings, there are none other than who are entitled to the rights in the compensation except the petitioners herein, the petitioners ought not to be prejudiced.

6. Accordingly, the following:-
ORDER i) The impugned General Award at Annexures-'G' and 'G1' dated 11.09.2018 passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB are set aside and are to be NC:
2023:KHC:21141 substituted by package compensation offered by BMRCL/KIADB.
Sri. Balaji.

4 ii)
The Reference Court to dispose of the Reference Petitions expeditiously.
iii) The package compensation offered by BMRCL is to be deposited by KIADB before the Reference Court within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent KIADB submits that the amount deposited by BMRCL has been diverted for other similar purpose.
8. This is a matter however to be reconciled between KIADB and BMRCL within a period of six weeks as stated hereinabove.

Insofar as the award amount deposited before the Reference Court as per the General Award, the same is to be taken note of and the remaining amount of compensation is to be deposited in terms of the package compensation.
Upon such deposit of compensation as directed hereinabove, the Reference Court is directed to invest the amount in any Nationalized Bank.

In the event, the petitioners succeed before the Reference Court, the Reference Court shall release/disburse the entire package amount of compensation alongwith the accrued interest in favour of the petitioners.

However, if the petitioners are not successful before the Reference Court, the amount so deposited by KIADB shall be refunded back while retaining the amount equivalent to General Award.
10.
It is submitted by the learned counsel appearing for BMRCL that there other litigations.
However, it is open for the BMRCL to bring the said fact to the notice of Reference Court, which may take note of it appropriately.

It is made clear that, in the event, the rights of petitioners is not recognized in the reference proceedings and some other persons are entitled, needless to state that,
if such of the other persons have not made any request for package compensation, they would be bound by the General Award, while keeping upon the rights to assail the same if the compensation is on the lower side.
Insofar as the petitioners herein are concerned, they would be entitled to the amount fixed in the package scheme and would not be entitled for enhancement.
Accordingly, the petition is disposed off.
